C2: NS-1(iii) fails: the GPS record shows the driver spent only 2 min 30 s within 200 m of the pickup before cancelling, which is under the required > 3 minutes (180 s). [F2 F4] [NS-1]
C3: The timeline confirms the short wait: the platform recorded arrival at 14:12:20 and the driver cancelled at 14:14:50, only 2 min 30 s later. [F5] [NS-1]
C4: The driver's own message 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which show 2 min 30 s inside the pickup radius, and the system records win over the statement. [F11 F2 F5] [NS-1 NS-2]

C7: The rider should also be granted the account-review flag: the driver pressed 'I'm Here' while stationary 41 m away, claimed a 3-minute wait his GPS data contradicts, and cancelled to trigger a fee — conduct Ryde classifies as abuse of the cancellation and waiting buttons. [F6 F3 F2 F11 F12] [NS-2 RD-6]
Weaknesses: The driver did in fact come close and stop: closest approach 38 m (F1) and stationary 41 m from the pickup for 2 minutes (F3), so the rider, not the driver, was the one not present at the pickup point. | The driver did genuinely tap 'I'm Here' (F6) and did message the rider at 14:13 (F10), so the driver's account that he arrived and waited is partially corroborated — the dispute turns solely on the 3-minute threshold, not on total absence. | The discrepancy between timeline records F6 (driver pressed 'I'm Here' at 14:13:10) and F7 (driver never tapped 'I'm Here') means the platform's own data is internally inconsistent on this point, which the other side may use to argue the arrival timestamp itself is unreliable. | The rider's evidence of her own readiness is thin: the profile shows a prior dispute with 0 upheld in 90 days (F16) and there is no app/GPS fact showing the rider approaching the pickup before 14:14:50.
Asks: refund_full $6.61

→ D5: I do not seek any penalty on the driver; the single request is the $6.61 refund, and the clean 90-day profiles (F16, F17) simply confirm no aggravating history is needed to decide this. [F16 F17] [NS-2]

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.86)
events.body:
The cancellation was driver-initiated at 14:14:50 and the $6.61 fee was recorded against the rider, so NS-0 routes the dispute through the NS-1 / NS-2 branch for a driver-claimed no-show [F4][F8][NS-0]. The cancellation policy applies because this is an ordinary RydeX trip, not RydeTAXI [F4][NS-0].

NS-1 has three cumulative conditions. Condition (i) is met: the timeline records a genuine "I'm Here" tap at 14:13:10 [F6], corroborated by the driver's arrival message at 14:13 [F10]. Condition (ii) is met: at the moment of the tap the driver was 39 m from the pickup, and his closest approach overall was 38 m, both well inside the pickup radius [F6][F1]. I treat the arrival-confirmation condition as satisfied despite F7's null field, because the contemporaneous platform timestamp in F6 is the more specific record and the rider advocate itself concedes (ii) [F6][F7][NS-1].

Condition (iii) fails. The system record shows the driver was within 200 m of the pickup from 14:12:20 until the 14:14:50 cancellation, a cumulative 2 min 30 s, and only 1 min 40 s inside the radius after the tap — both short of the required > 3 minutes (180 s, i.e. ≥ 3:01) [F2][F6][F4][F5]. The driver's stationary period was just 2 min 0 s [F3]. The driver's chat claim of having waited "more than 3 min" is a statement and yields to the GPS and timeline records on this point [F11][NS-1].

Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) is not satisfied in full, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee to be refunded in full to the rider; the arithmetic is simply the fee on record, $6.61, and NS-7 directs that it be issued as a Ryde voucher [F8][F4][NS-2][NS-7]. Route and traffic conditions are irrelevant here — no off-route segments or incidents appear, and RD-1/RD-4 are not engaged [F13][F14].

No account flag is warranted. NS-2's flag attaches only where the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius; here he was 39 m away at the tap and stationary 41 m from the pickup for 2 minutes, and his 90-day record shows 0 upheld disputes over 571 trips, so the abuse precondition and the RD-6 "repeated" precondition are both absent [F6][F1][F3][F17][NS-2][RD-6].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); no account flag on the driver — the wait fell 30 s short of the 3-minute threshold, but the tap was genuine and within the pickup radius.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled on the rider and the system charged the $6.61 cancellation fee, so this dispute is governed by NS-0 / NS-1 / NS-2 (driver-initiated no-show cancellation).
NS-1(iii) fails: the GPS record shows the driver spent only 2 min 30 s within 200 m of the pickup before cancelling, which is under the required > 3 minutes (180 s).
The timeline confirms the short wait: the platform recorded arrival at 14:12:20 and the driver cancelled at 14:14:50, only 2 min 30 s later.

The driver's own message 'Waited more than 3 min, cancelling' is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records, which show 2 min 30 s inside the pickup radius, and the system records win over the statement.
The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 14:13:10 and then stayed within 200 m for only 1 min 40 s, so even measured from the tap the 3-minute waiting requirement is not met.
Because NS-1 (iii) is not satisfied, the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full to the rider.

The rider should also be granted the account-review flag: the driver pressed 'I'm Here' while stationary 41 m away, claimed a 3-minute wait his GPS data contradicts, and cancelled to trigger a fee — conduct Ryde classifies as abuse of the cancellation and waiting buttons.

weaknesses: The driver did in fact come close and stop: closest approach 38 m (F1) and stationary 41 m from the pickup for 2 minutes (F3), so the rider, not the driver, was the one not present at the pickup point.

The driver did genuinely tap 'I'm Here' (F6) and did message the rider at 14:13 (F10), so the driver's account that he arrived and waited is partially corroborated — the dispute turns solely on the 3-minute threshold, not on total absence.

The discrepancy between timeline records F6 (driver pressed 'I'm Here' at 14:13:10) and F7 (driver never tapped 'I'm Here') means the platform's own data is internally inconsistent on this point, which the other side may use to argue the arrival timestamp itself is unreliable.

The rider's evidence of her own readiness is thin: the profile shows a prior dispute with 0 upheld in 90 days (F16) and there is no app/GPS fact showing the rider approaching the pickup before 14:14:50.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here": the timeline records the tap at 14:13:10 with the driver 39 m from the pickup point, and his own chat message #1 at 14:13 says he is at the pickup point in a grey Kia Niro.

The driver was at the pickup location according to GPS when he pressed "I'm Here" and throughout the wait: closest approach 38 m, stationary 14:12:50-14:14:50 at 41 m from pickup, and he remained within 200 m for 1 min 40 s after the tap, so the within-200 m condition of NS-1(ii) is satisfied.

The driver's GPS presence within 200 m of the pickup runs from 14:12:20 to the 14:14:50 cancellation, i.e. 2 min 30 s, which is short of the >3 min (181 s) threshold NS-1(iii) requires, so strictly on the system record the $6.61 does not stand on NS-1 — but this is a 30-second shortfall, not a driver fault: the platform itself recorded arrival at 14:12:20 (F5) while the rider never appeared.

The rider was charged $6.61 as cancellation fee (F8) but the driver, who made the trip to the pickup point and waited, receives only $4.50 of it; the driver has no windfall from the charge and no overcharge is alleged against him.

No aggravation exists on the driver's record or in the trip data: the driver has 571 trips in 90 days with 0 upheld disputes (F17), the rider has 0 upheld no-show disputes (F16), and the cancellation is a single, non-surge event (F9) with no route deviation facts returned.

The rider's complaint that the driver cancelled "after barely two minutes" is contradicted by the timeline: the driver accepted at 14:09:00 and cancelled at 14:14:50, 5 min 50 s later, after spending 2 min 30 s inside the 200 m pickup radius.

weaknesses: NS-1(iii) requires cumulative waiting at the pickup of more than 3 minutes, and the system record shows F2 (2 min 30 s within 200 m) and F3 (stationary only 2 min 0 s before cancellation) — a 30-second shortfall that the rider will rely on, along with F7 vs F6, to argue the fee does not attach.

The timeline is internally inconsistent on the "I'm Here" tap: F7 states the driver never tapped it (driver_pressed_here_at is null) while F6 records a tap at 14:13:10, and the rider will cite F7 rather than the driver's own chat statement F12, since statements lose to platform records.

The driver's chat message #2 (F11, "Waited more than 3 min, cancelling") is itself inaccurate on the system timeline (F5: cancelled 2 min 30 s after recorded arrival), which the rider can use to attack the driver's credibility on the wait duration.

points.response: The tap is not decisive: NS-1 requires all three of (i) tap, (ii) GPS presence and (iii) more than 3 minutes waiting, and the driver's own evidence F6 shows only 1 min 40 s within 200 m after the 14:13:10 tap, so the condition in NS-1(iii) still fails.
I accept NS-1(ii) is met: closest approach 38 m (F1) and stationary at 41 m (F3) place the driver within the pickup radius, so my case rests entirely on NS-1(iii), not on (ii).

The 30-second shortfall is the whole point: NS-1(iii) sets a hard '> 3 minutes' threshold and the system record gives 2 min 30 s (F2) with only 2 min 0 s stationary (F3), so under NS-2 the fee must be refunded in full — 'close enough' is not a condition in NS-1, and the driver's own F11 message claiming 'more than 3 min' shows the wait was miscounted.

Whether the driver keeps $4.50 or not is irrelevant to the rider's liability: NS-2 makes the $6.61 refundable when NS-1's conditions are unmet, and NS-7 requires the refund to be issued as a voucher in that amount regardless of the driver's split.
I do not seek any penalty on the driver; the single request is the $6.61 refund, and the clean 90-day profiles (F16, F17) simply confirm no aggravating history is needed to decide this.

The 'barely two minutes' in the complaint refers to the time the driver actually waited at the pickup, and the system record supports that: 2 min 30 s inside 200 m (F2) and 2 min 0 s stationary (F3) before the 14:14:50 cancellation (F4).

Conceded: the cancellation was driver-initiated and the $6.61 is on record, so NS-0 routes the dispute through NS-1/NS-2 — but NS-2 only refunds where NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) fails, and (i) and (ii) are met here.

The 2 min 30 s figure in F2 measures presence within the 200 m radius only from 14:12:20, but the driver had already stopped 41 m from the pickup at 14:12:50 (F3) and tapped "I'm Here" at 14:13:10 (F6); the shortfall against the 180 s threshold is 30 seconds, which is within the granularity of the recorded arrival (F5) and does not show the driver failed to wait.

F5 confirms the platform itself recorded arrival at 14:12:20, and the cancellation followed at 14:14:50 (F4); on the rider's own numbers the driver spent the entire interval at the pickup point having already driven there, which is the conduct NS-1 protects, not the abuse NS-2 punishes.

The driver's chat wording (F11) may be loose, but it is corroborated by F6 (tap at 14:13:10, 39 m out) and F10 ("I'm here at the pickup point" at 14:13), so the driver's arrival and wait are system-recorded facts, not a bare statement; the 30-second discrepancy cannot convert a genuine, GPS-verified wait into a fabricated one.

Conceded as arithmetic: measured from the 14:13:10 tap, F6 shows only 1 min 40 s inside 200 m, so NS-1(iii) is not strictly satisfied — but the same record shows the driver waiting continuously at 41 m from 14:12:50 (F3) with the rider never arriving (F16: no upheld no-show history, no rider-approach fact), so at most the fee is waived as a threshold technicality.

The refund of $6.61 under NS-2 is arithmetically driven by a 30-second shortfall on a record the platform itself generated inconsistently (F6 vs F7 on whether "I'm Here" was pressed), so the driver does not resist a waiver on the threshold; what the evidence does not support is any finding that he fabricated the wait.

The abuse flag under NS-2 requires that the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS showed he was NOT at the pickup (within_200m false), whereas here he was 39 m away at the tap (F6) and stationary 41 m for 2 minutes (F3); the profile shows 0 upheld disputes and 571 trips in 90 days (F17) with no repeated conduct, so no flag_account on RD-6 either.
